reports.title: Lake Russell fishing report
reports.text:
Black bass: Guide Jerry Kotal (706-988-0860) reports that in November bass should be out deep around bait schools on both the main lake and in the creeks. They will be caught on jigging spoons once temperatures cool, and soft plastics before that, for anglers who do not want to fish live bait.
Crappie: Guide Wendell Wilson reports that November should continue to be a good time for Lake Russell crappie – as long as you can locate fish. This can be more of a challenge than at other times of year because many will relate to moving bait schools rather than simply cover. But they are hungry and will eat both minnows and jigs when found.

reports.title: Clarks Hill (Lake Thurmond) fishing report
reports.text:
Black bass: Guide Josh Rockefeller (706-513-6152) and tournament angler Tyler Matthews report that in November fish should continue to make their move back into the creeks – although some will stay offshore on the main lake. For shallow water fishermen square-billed crankbaits should work well around natural rock, and it can also be a good time for flipping jigs around creek docks that still have water on them. Especially at the beginning of the month continue to look out for schooling fish, but then expect subsurface offshore patterns to be dominant for fish feeding on bait schools.

reports.title: Lake Wylie fishing report
reports.text:
Bass bass: Tournament angler Reid McGinn of Fort Mill reports that in November more and more fish should move into the creeks as temperatures continue to cool, although plenty of spotted bass will stay on the main lake. The bite should transition from a topwater bite to crankbaits, swimbaits, jigging spoons, and more.
Crappie: Captain Chris Nichols (704-860-7951) reports that at the end of October crappie could be found both shallow around structure and deeper in the channels, and in November this pattern should hold until it gets colder and the majority of the fish head deep. reports.source: South Carolina DNR freshwater fishing trends
reports.title: Lake Greenwood fishing report
reports.text:
Black bass: Veteran tournament angler Stan Gunter of Greenwood reports that in November bass fishing should continue to improve on Lake Greenwood, and more fish should move into the creeks following bait schools. At the beginning of the month most fish were still relating to the main lake as the bait had not migrated back. Rattle Traps and spinnerbaits should both catch fish this month, and there could be some schooling activity.
Crappie: Captain Roland Addy (864-980-3672) reports that in November fish will be around structure near the main river channel or major creek channels if bait moves into the creeks. Bridge pilings, brush, stumps, and trees can all produce. Down the lake fish will…

reports.source: South Carolina DNR freshwater fishing trends
reports.title: Lake Monticello fishing report
reports.text: Black bass: BYA Fishing’s Eric Enlow of Union reports that in early November fishing topwater lures can still be effective, especially early. However, later in the month he will almost exclusively be fishing a spoon around deep bait schools – or chasing roaming fish offshore with a minnow-type bait.

reports.source: South Carolina DNR freshwater fishing trends
reports.title: Lake Murray fishing report
reports.text:
Black Bass: Tournament angler Andy Wicker of Pomaria reports that in November the fishing should improve after the fall turnover settles out. Some fish will stay suspended on offshore structure and start taking a jerkbait or underspin, while some fish will move shallow and relate to the sides of rocky points and areas with hard bottom. A shaky head worm can be very good this month, but if bait is around, va #5 Shad Rap fished in small ditches and pockets can also work well. There will also be another group of fish that can be caught on the bottom deep.
Crappie: Captain Brad Taylor reports that up the lake in November some fish will move off of brush and start to follow bait in open water…

reports.source: South Carolina DNR freshwater fishing trends
reports.title: Lake Wateree fishing report
reports.text:
Black bass: Tournament angler Dearal Rodgers of Camden reports that in November the bite is almost all about where the bait schools are located. With high water levels and dropping temperatures to start the month the creeks were holding a lot of shad. Bass will relate to points that are near the bait, and shad-colored crankbaits, lipless crankbaits, and spinnerbaits will all catch fish. Shaky heads around docks will also usually produce.

reports.source: South Carolina DNR freshwater fishing trends
reports.title: Santee Cooper fishing report
reports.text:
Black bass: Captain David Murdaugh Sr. (843-452-9566) reports that when it finally gets cooler in November more fish will start to follow shad. In addition to soft plastics, swimbaits and crankbaits will produce in shallow water. Fish should also continue to be caught offshore on brush and around grass.
Crappie and Bream: Captain Steve English (843-729-4044) reports that this November the bite should be good for both species around mid-depth brush. The lakes will produce crappie fishing vertically with minnows, and there are very positive signs from this fall about the state of the population. reports.source: South Carolina DNR freshwater fishing trends
reports.title: Lake Jocassee fishing report
reports.text: Trout and black bass: Guide Sam Jones (864-280-9056) reports that November is usually about the toughest month for trout fishing on Lake Jocassee, but since they were still catching trout throughout October optimism is high for a decent month. Since Jocassee cools slowly trout should still be deep well into November, and trolling in deeper water with spoons or live bait is generally the preferred technique. But the main catch is expected to be spotted bass, and this fall they have been picking up good numbers of spots while targeting trout with their deep lines as well as shallower lines geared towards bass. reports.source: South Carolina DNR freshwater fishing trends
reports.title: Lake Keowee fishing report
reports.text: Black Bass: Guide Charles Townson (864-324-2065) reports that anglers should continue to look out for schooling activity in November, particularly earlier in the month, but in late October the fish were already starting to move into the creeks and subsurface patterns were becoming dominant. This month shaky heads should produce around structure for shallower fish and drop shots will work for deeper fish following bait schools. Most detailed Lake Keowee Updates

reports.source: South Carolina DNR freshwater fishing trends
reports.title: Lake Hartwell fishing report
reports.text:
Black Bass: Guide Lane Clark (864-254-8614) reports that in November fish should be eating bait in the creeks, and while they are unlikely to be feeding on the surface as much as last month they will often still take a bait fished higher in the water column like a swimbait or jerkbait. Drop shots and shaky heads fished around brush will also work for spotted bass. Low water levels have fish more concentrated than usual, and this is making for a very strong fall.
